reason: The passage portrays Moses taking protective and authoritative action on behalf of his Hebrew brethren. He goes out to witness their burdens, defends one Hebrew from Egyptian violence, and attempts to judge a dispute between two Hebrews. Most significantly, when Moses confronts a Hebrew wrongdoer, the man directly challenges him with the question: 'Who made thee a prince and a judge over us?' (שַׂר וְשֹׁפֵט — sar ve-shophet). This explicit invocation of leadership titles demonstrates that Moses is portrayed as aspiring to leadership roles — as a chief and judge of his people — even though these attempts are premature and ultimately unsuccessful, forcing him to flee Egypt. The text establishes Moses as one who identifies with his people's suffering and assumes an authoritative role on their behalf.
